chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban, from 'Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'We do not consider an ablution (wudu) to be required for the seminal fluid (madhi), nor a ritual bath (ghusl) for whatever of it hits the garment, except for the great water (semen/madh').

key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْأَكْبَرِ: The great water, referring to semen (maniy), which requires ghusl.
key_terms.الْمَذْيِ: Seminal fluid (madhi), a lighter fluid released during arousal, distinguished from semen.
key_terms.غَسْلًا: Ritual bath (ghusl), the major ritual washing required for major impurity.
key_terms.وُضُوءاً: Ablution (wudu), the minor ritual washing required for prayer.

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual purity ruling for seminal fluid (madhi) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the ruling for *madhi* (pre-seminal fluid), clarifying that it does not necessitate *wudu* or *ghusl* due to its minor nature, unlike *maniy* (semen). This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that purity obligations are proportional to the substance's volume and type, requiring only washing the soiled area of clothing rather than a full ritual bath.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban, from Anbasa Bin Mus’ab who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Weasws do not view an Ablution (Wudhu) to be regarding the seminal fluid, nor a washing in whatever hits the clothes from it, except regarding the great water (semen)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Aban from ‘Anbasah ibn Mus’ab who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘Wudu’ is not necessary because of al-Madhiy (the pre-seminal fluid) nor is washing clothes which may have come in contact with it unless it is the major discharge of (semen).”’
